evals.prompt: Pull the full population time series for California and Texas from Data Commons so I can plot how they've grown since 2000.
evals.expected_output: Triggers the Data Commons skill without asking for an API key. Resolves the place names to DCIDs (geoId/06 for California, geoId/48 for Texas) via the keyless v2 resolve endpoint (scripts/query_datacommons.py resolve, or client.resolve.fetch_dcids_by_name), then pulls Count_Person with date='all' — the keyless website series endpoint (query_datacommons.py observe Count_Person geoId/06 geoId/48 --date all --csv) or, with a DC_API_KEY, client.observation.fetch(date='all') — and loads the tidy records into a Pandas DataFrame pivoted on date for plotting, covering at least 2000 onward (2020: California 39,527,808 per the Census PEP facet) and citing the provenance (USCensusPEP).

assertions.value: Resolves place names to DCIDs before querying observations rather than querying by raw name.
Uses the observation endpoint with date='all' to retrieve the full time series.

evals.prompt: I need median household income for every county in California in 2020 from Data Commons. Get them all in one go rather than county by county.
evals.expected_output: Triggers Data Commons without asking for an API key. Fetches Median_Income_Household for date='2020' for every county of California in a single hierarchy query — the keyless website point/within endpoint (query_datacommons.py within Median_Income_Household geoId/06 County --date 2020, the equivalent of the relation expression geoId/06<-containedInPlace+{typeOf:County}) or, with a DC_API_KEY, client.observation.fetch(entity_expression='geoId/06<-containedInPlace+{typeOf:County}') — returning all 58 counties (e.g. Alameda County geoId/06001: 104,888 USD, ACS 5-year) rather than looping county by county.

assertions.value: Fetches all counties of the state in one hierarchy query (the keyless point/within endpoint, or an entity relation expression with containedInPlace) rather than looping per county.

evals.prompt: I have a GPS coordinate (37.7749, -122.4194) and a couple of Wikidata IDs (Q30, Q99). What Data Commons entities do they map to?
evals.expected_output: Triggers Data Commons without asking for an API key. Uses the keyless v2 resolve endpoint: <-wikidataId->dcid maps Q30 to country/USA and Q99 to geoId/06 (California); for the GPS point it tries <-geoCoordinate->dcid (fetch_dcid_by_coordinates) and, when that returns no candidates, falls back to a keyless geocoder (US Census geocoder GEOIDs -> geoId/06, geoId/06075 San Francisco County, geoId/0667000 San Francisco city). Demonstrates entity identification rather than statistical retrieval, and says which route produced each DCID.

assertions.value: Uses the resolve endpoint's coordinate and Wikidata-ID resolution methods to map external identifiers to DCIDs.

evals.prompt: What is the latest unemployment rate for the United States according to Data Commons, and can you also check what statistical variables are even available for the country?
evals.expected_output: Triggers Data Commons. Resolves country/USA, calls client.observation.fetch with variable_dcids=['UnemploymentRate_Person'] and date='latest', and uses client.observation.fetch_available_statistical_variables(entity_dcids=['country/USA']) to enumerate queryable variables. Works keyless through the datacommons.org website API (observe UnemploymentRate_Person country/USA; vars-search / has for the variable check), reports the value with its YYYY-MM date and the BLS (BLS_CPS) provenance, and mentions DC_API_KEY only as the optional route to the documented v2 API.

assertions.value: Checks available statistical variables for the entity and queries the latest observation for the unemployment rate.

evals.prompt: According to Data Commons, what was Turkey's population in 2020, and which original source does that number come from? I don't have a Data Commons API key.
evals.expected_output: Triggers Data Commons and works keyless: resolves Turkey to country/TUR, queries Count_Person for date 2020 through the datacommons.org website API (scripts/query_datacommons.py observe Count_Person country/TUR --date 2020), and reports 83,384,680 for 2020 with its provenance — the World Bank World Development Indicators (provenanceId dc/base/WorldDevelopmentIndicators) — noting that the keyless route is the website's undocumented API and that a DC_API_KEY is optional.

assertions.value: Reports Turkey's 2020 population as about 83.4 million (83,384,680) and attributes it to the World Bank World Development Indicators, without requiring an API key.

evals.prompt: Find me all actively recruiting Phase 3 clinical trials for type 2 diabetes in the United States, with their NCT IDs and enrollment targets.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger Data Commons. This requests individual interventional clinical-trial records (NCT IDs, recruitment status, phase, enrollment) from the ClinicalTrials.gov registry, not aggregated public statistics. Data Commons serves statistical observations (population, GDP, disease prevalence counts) over geographic entities, not a trial registry. Defers to alterlab-clinicaltrials.

evals.prompt: How many papers on climate adaptation were published per year over the last decade, and what's the citation trend? I want a bibliometric breakdown.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger Data Commons. Counts of scholarly publications and citation trends over time are bibliometric data served by OpenAlex, not statistical observations over geographic/demographic entities. Data Commons aggregates census, economic, health, and environmental statistics, not literature metadata. Defers to alterlab-openalex.
